# LoCoMo offline arm, leave-one-conversation-out (generated by `python -m paper2.report`)

Code hash `1567a77400f9d79f`, data `data/raw/locomo/locomo10.json` sha256 `79fa87e90f040813…`, written 2026-10-19T15:15:35Z.
Learned gates are fitted on the other nine conversations (`paper2/out/w_loo/`), memory is matched by bisection to a fraction of each
conversation's admit-all live facts (tolerance 5%), retrieval is BM25 top-20 + 1-hop, value is evidence recall (no model calls).

primary: exact sign-flip permutation on the k per-conversation mean differences (all 2^k assignments enumerated; two-sided); smallest attainable p = 2/2^k = 0.0020 for k=10. The 95% t-interval has k-1 df (t quantile by numerical inversion, not scipy; --selftest checks it against the table).
Holm: applied to the family of 8 permutation p-values in this invocation (merged_loo_graph_gate_struct_m0.5 vs each other run, metric hit). This is the command-line family, not the pre-registered four-hypothesis family (critique C8); per-category and per-budget comparisons are exploratory and should be reported as intervals.
cluster-boot CI95: cluster (conversation) bootstrap of the pooled mean difference; an interval, not a test (at most 92378 distinct resamples for k=10).
question-boot CI95: question-level paired bootstrap; secondary, anti-conservative (questions within a conversation are not independent).
mean = unweighted mean of the per-conversation differences; the pooled question-level mean is in the JSON output (--json) as cluster.mean. bootstraps: 2000 resamples, seed 0.

## 4. Poisoning arm (H4), fabricated facts injected with probability 10% per dialogue turn (about a quarter of the candidate stream), memory = 50%

`sourceless`: poison carries the same tier confidence as real candidates (no policy can see it). Injection is per dialogue turn at 10%, two copies each, i.e. about a quarter of the candidate stream (the draft's earlier wording "10% of candidate turns" was wrong; corrected 22 Oct). `lower`: poison tier 0.4 vs 0.6. `_tier`: the
policy score is multiplied by mean tier confidence. The injected set is identical across policies.

## 6. Interpretation (hand-written, 18 Oct 2026, from sections 1–5 above)

**What the LoCoMo offline arm supports.** At matched memory size with gates fitted leave-one-out, the
structural-only gate (seven graph features, no turn length, no recency, no observation count) retains
more evidence than random, than the 2010 product, than Impact alone and than both A-MAC-feature
policies, in 8 to 10 of 10 conversations, with exact permutation p ≤ 0.008 and Holm-corrected p ≤ 0.031
(section 3). At half the memory it keeps 67% of admit-all's evidence-hit (0.431 / 0.643); random keeps
59%, the 2010 product 50%. The 2010 Trust × Impact product is the worst policy at every budget: Trust is
exactly 0 on 77% of candidates and 1 on 6%, so the product can only prefer repetition, and Impact alone
inherits the speaker-hub dominance (section 5). This degeneracy is now measured under an entity layer
that gives 13% of non-hub vertices degree ≥ 2, so it is a property of the published formulas at fact
granularity, not only of a bad extractor (critique B(iv) separated the two; both contribute).

**What it does not support.** The structural gate does not reliably beat the length + revisit heuristic
(+0.027, t-interval touching zero, Holm p = 0.146, 8/10 conversations); that heuristic is essentially
turn length, the single strongest label correlate (AUC 0.63, section 5). Adding the surface features to
the structural gate changes nothing (−0.004), so the structural features and turn length carry
overlapping information about what annotators asked about. The hand-set prior gate is weaker than the
fitted structural-only gate (−0.022, n.s.) and no better than heat. The claim the paper can make is
therefore: *an LLM-free gate over graph features beats random, the 2010 measures and A-MAC-style lexical
features at matched size, and matches a length heuristic*, not that structure beats everything.

**Structure, honestly.** Every memory in this arm is still two speaker stars with repeated leaves: 0.0%
of edges join two non-hub vertices in every conversation (section 1). The "structural" features
therefore measure recurrence of objects around the speakers, not graph topology, and the wording in the
paper must follow critique E1's fallback: turn-level admission features over an entity-centric fact
store. Entity-to-entity edges need an extractor that emits non-speaker subjects, which on this dataset
means the LLM arm.

**SIVa.** The 2010 SIVa (unweighted new-edge ratio) and the degree-weighted consolidation-aware
redesign are rank-identical (ρ = 0.99) because consolidation never fires: after the type-guarded
extractor repair the functional rule finds 8 true functional facts in 2,549 and 0 contradictions in the
whole corpus (section 1, `invalidated` column). Both are clocks (ρ with position −0.83 / −0.82); the
size-invariant `siva_scaled` is not (−0.07) and is the quantity to use in the H2 model, with log|Ec| and
position as covariates. H2 and the consolidation claim are untestable on LoCoMo observations and move
to LongMemEval-S knowledge-update questions and the LLM-extraction arm, as pre-registration log items
12–13 already state.

**Poisoning (H4).** With fabricated facts drawn from the real predicate distribution, verbalised with
their predicate, repeated once and carrying the same tier confidence as real candidates (`sourceless`),
the structural gates admit *more* poison than random (34% / 32% vs 29%) and the tier multiplier has, by
construction, no effect. When the poison carries a lower provenance tier (`lower`) and the score is
multiplied by tier confidence, poison admission falls to 10% for both gates (random with the multiplier:
19%) and evidence-hit rises from 0.300 to 0.403 (structural-only) and 0.320 to 0.378 (prior), because
poison stops displacing real facts within the same budget (section 4). The paper's statement is that
structural novelty is blind to truth and that provenance weighting is the defence; the orthogonality is
the result, and the `sourceless` condition is the honest ceiling on what an attacker who can forge the
provenance route achieves. Nearly every question retrieves at least one poison fact at this injection
rate (10% of turns, two copies each), so retrieval-level harm needs the online arm.

**Per category** (admit-all ceiling): temporal 0.72, adversarial 0.65, multi-hop 0.64, single-hop 0.64,
open-domain 0.43 (n = 89); multi-hop `frac` is 0.34 against `hit` 0.64, i.e. the retrieved set usually
holds one of the gold turns, rarely all. Per-category gate comparisons are exploratory (intervals, no
p-values) under the pre-registered four-family rule.

**What changes in the plan.** (1) Headline policy: structural-only gate × tier confidence; heat is the
baseline to beat, reported as "turn length + revisit". (2) The claim of superiority over heuristics is
dropped from the title and H1 wording unless LongMemEval-S and the online arm show it. (3) H2, H3 and
the consolidation claim run on LongMemEval-S and the LLM arm only. (4) Before any F1 number: the online
arm on admit-all and two gated memories to validate evidence-hit against answer quality (critique
B(vi)). (5) The ESWC workshop or poster target stands; the research-track deadline (17 Dec 2026) is
not realistic with the online arm still to run.

## 7. Online arm and the Mem0 baseline (19 Oct 2026; runs `merged_online2_*`, `merged_h1_*`, analyses in `proxy_pass2_analysis.txt`, `out/h1_mem0.log`)

Answerer: Claude Haiku 5.5, thinking off, official LoCoMo scoring, facts carried with their session date
and the official temporal hint (pass 2; pass 1 without dates is in `proxy_pass1_analysis.txt`).

| memory | evidence-hit | token F1 | EM | abstained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| admit all (2,618 facts) | 0.643 | 0.491 | 0.343 | 0.469 |
| structural-only gate, 50% | 0.431 | 0.408 | 0.304 | 0.617 |
| random, 50% | 0.379 | 0.388 | 0.290 | 0.622 |

- **The proxy carries signal but halves the gate's effect.** F1 is 0.57 when a gold fact was retrieved
  and 0.30 when not (+0.27 pooled; +0.47 single-hop, +0.31 temporal, +0.18 multi-hop, −0.00 adversarial).
  Per-conversation differences structural-minus-random agree in sign for hit and F1 in 7 of 10
  conversations (Spearman 0.92), but the F1 gain is +0.026 [−0.002, +0.054], permutation p = 0.064,
  against +0.057 in evidence-hit. The paper reports both and calls evidence-hit an optimistic proxy.
- **Dates matter.** Without the session date on each fact, temporal F1 was 0.06 under admit-all; with it,
  0.32. Any memory system evaluated on LoCoMo without timestamps on facts is handicapped on a quarter
  of the questions.
- **Mem0's verbatim gate does not gate here.** Mem0 v1.0.11's ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NONE prompt admits
  97.5% of candidate turns (memory 98.6% of admit-all) at 742 model calls per 1,000 candidates. At that
  size the structural gate (F1 0.490, hit 0.640), Mem0 (0.488, 0.638) and random (0.481, 0.623) are
  within noise. H1 therefore holds trivially (+0.011 F1 inside the 2-point margin) and the honest
  statement is that an LLM gate run on pre-distilled observations has nothing to reject; the comparison
  that matters is at a real budget, where Mem0 has no knob.

**Plan, revised 19 Oct.** (1) The headline is unchanged: the LLM-free gate beats random, the 2010
measures and A-MAC features at matched size and matches a length heuristic; F1 confirms the direction
with half the size. (2) H1 is reported as answered trivially on LoCoMo, with the budgeted comparison as
the real test. (3) Topology is a benchmark property (`09-nonspeaker-subjects.md`: 2.3% non-speaker
subjects), so LongMemEval-S is the only place H2, H3 and entity-to-entity structure can be tested.
(4) Target: ESWC 2027 workshop; arXiv preprint as soon as the metadata TODOs are filled.

## 8. LongMemEval-S, first offline numbers (20 Oct 2026; run `lme_s_admit_all_100`, heuristic extractor, no model calls)

First 100 questions of LongMemEval-S (cleaned), one memory per question built from its own haystack
(38 to 62 sessions), candidates = first-person sentences of user turns, admit everything.

| | value |
|---|---|
| questions | 100 (64 single-session-user, 30 multi-session, 6 other) |
| candidate facts per question (mean) | 404; live after admission 333 |
| total live facts | 33,270 (LoCoMo, all 10 conversations: 2,618) |
| evidence-hit | 0.617 [0.521, 0.713]; multi-session 0.733, single-session-user 0.562 |
| evidence fraction / MRR | 0.514 / about 0.41 |
| admission precision / recall against has_answer turns | 0.01 / 0.95 |
| share of non-hub vertices with degree ≥ 2; non-hub-to-non-hub edges | 0.05–0.10; 0.00 |

Reading: on LongMemEval-S a memory that admits everything holds about 13 times more facts per
question than on LoCoMo, and only one candidate in a hundred is evidence, so admission control has
stakes here that it does not have on LoCoMo. The star shape persists under the heuristic extractor
because its subjects are the user; entity-to-entity edges need the LLM-extraction arm
(`09-nonspeaker-subjects.md` section 4 measured 15.5% of user turns with two third-party entities).
Next: matched-size runs of the prior-weight gate, heat and random on the same 100 questions (no
LoCoMo-fitted weights, so no transfer leakage), then the LLM arm when a key is available.

### 8.1 Matched size, 50% of admit-all, same 100 questions (runs `lme_s_{graph_gate,random,heat}_m0.5_100`; no LoCoMo-fitted weights)

| policy | live facts | evidence-hit [95% q-CI] | frac | MRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| structural gate, prior weights | 16,630 | **0.362** [0.266, 0.457] | 0.265 | 0.295 |
| random | 16,642 | 0.309 [0.223, 0.404] | 0.226 | 0.231 |
| length + revisit heuristic | 16,694 | 0.202 [0.128, 0.277] | 0.142 | 0.171 |
| admit all | 33,270 | 0.617 | 0.514 | 0.411 |

Paired per-question tests (94 questions with gold evidence; the question is the independent unit here):
gate vs heat +0.160 [+0.046, +0.273], permutation p = 0.010, 23 wins / 8 losses; gate vs random +0.053
[−0.065, +0.171], p = 0.47, 18 / 13; random vs heat +0.106, p = 0.072. On MRR:
```
       lme_s_random_m0.5_100  94  +0.064   [-0.035,+0.163]   0.206  0.206 [-0.034,+0.163] [-0.034,+0.162]     20/16     20/94
         lme_s_heat_m0.5_100  94  +0.124   [+0.026,+0.221]   0.013  0.026 [+0.021,+0.221] [+0.027,+0.223]     24/8      24/94
```
Reading: the turn-length heuristic that matched the structural gate on LoCoMo is *below random* on
LongMemEval-S (long user turns in a 50-session haystack are rarely the evidence), while the structural
gate stays above random by about the LoCoMo margin. With 100 binary outcomes the gate-vs-random
difference is not yet significant; the 500-question run is in progress. These numbers use the prior
weights, i.e. no fitting at all, so there is no leakage from LoCoMo.

### 8.2 All 500 questions, memory = 50% (runs `lme_s_*_500`; prior weights, heuristic extractor, no fitting)

| policy | live facts | evidence-hit [95% q-CI] | frac | MRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| admit all | 167,482 | 0.574 [0.530, 0.618] | 0.411 | 0.362 |
| structural gate, prior weights | 83,679 | **0.334** [0.292, 0.378] | 0.212 | 0.249 |
| random | 83,784 | 0.326 [0.284, 0.367] | 0.202 | 0.211 |
| length + revisit heuristic | 83,786 | 0.244 [0.207, 0.284] | 0.143 | 0.172 |

Paired per-question tests over the 479 questions with gold evidence (sign-flip permutation, two-sided):

| comparison | evidence-hit | MRR | frac |
|---|---|---|---|
| gate − random | +0.008 [−0.040, +0.056], p = 0.80 | +0.038 [−0.001, +0.077], p = 0.057 | +0.011, p = 0.53 |
| gate − heat | +0.090 [+0.040, +0.139], p < 0.001 | +0.077 [+0.036, +0.117], p < 0.001 | +0.070, p < 0.001 |
| random − heat | +0.081 [+0.036, +0.127], p = 0.001 | +0.039 [+0.003, +0.075], p = 0.033 | +0.059, p < 0.001 |

Per type (hit, admit-all / gate / random / heat): knowledge-update 0.69 / 0.33 / 0.36 / 0.28;
multi-session 0.73 / 0.45 / 0.44 / 0.31; single-session-user 0.56 / 0.33 / 0.25 / 0.13;
temporal-reasoning 0.56 / 0.35 / 0.33 / 0.30; single-session-preference 0.53 / 0.33 / 0.30 / 0.17;
single-session-assistant 0.14 / 0.05 / 0.11 / 0.11 (assistant turns are not candidates for this extractor).

**Reading, and this supersedes 8.1.** The 100-question lead of the gate over random (+0.053) was sampling
noise: over 500 questions the unfitted structural gate is level with random on evidence-hit (+0.008)
and only marginally ahead on rank (MRR +0.038, p = 0.057). What holds is the negative result about the
length heuristic: it is 8 to 9 points *below random* on every metric (p ≤ 0.001), so "matches a
turn-length heuristic" on LoCoMo was a statement about LoCoMo's annotators, not about the gate. The
LoCoMo advantage of the gate over random does not transfer to LongMemEval-S with hand-set prior
weights and first-person-sentence candidates; whether a gate fitted on LongMemEval-S itself (5-fold by
question, structural features only) does better is the next run. Single-session-assistant questions
are near zero for every policy because the heuristic extractor ignores assistant turns: an extractor
limit, to be fixed in the LLM arm.

### 8.3 Gate fitted on LongMemEval-S itself, 5-fold by question (runs `lme_s_graph_gate_struct_m0.5_fold*`, merged in `lme_s_graph_gate_struct_m0.5_500`; weights `paper2/out/w_lme/`)

Structural features only (the seven in `measures.STRUCTURAL`), fitted on the admit-all candidate turns
of the other 400 questions for each fold (grouped CV AUC 0.69–0.71; largest weights impact ≈ +1.0,
novelty ≈ +0.35, soft agreement ≈ +0.15 in every fold), evaluated at 50% matched memory on the held-out
100. No LoCoMo weights are used anywhere.

| policy (500 questions, memory = 50%) | live facts | evidence-hit [95% q-CI] | frac | MRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **structural-only gate, fitted 5-fold** | 84,038 | **0.399** [0.355, 0.443] | 0.262 | 0.291 |
| structural gate, prior weights | 83,679 | 0.334 | 0.212 | 0.249 |
| random | 83,784 | 0.326 | 0.202 | 0.211 |
| length + revisit heuristic | 83,786 | 0.244 | 0.143 | 0.172 |
| admit all | 167,482 | 0.574 | 0.411 | 0.362 |

Paired per-question tests, 479 questions with gold evidence, Holm over the three comparisons:

| fitted gate − … | evidence-hit | MRR |
|---|---|---|
| random | +0.073 [+0.027, +0.119], p = 0.003 (Holm 0.005), 81 wins / 46 | +0.080 [+0.043, +0.117], p < 0.001 |
| prior-weight gate | +0.065 [+0.024, +0.105], p = 0.003 (Holm 0.005) | +0.043 [+0.008, +0.077], p = 0.015 |
| length heuristic | +0.154 [+0.106, +0.203], p < 0.001 | +0.119 [+0.077, +0.161], p < 0.001 |

Per type (hit): multi-session 0.58, knowledge-update 0.49, temporal-reasoning 0.41, single-session-preference
0.30, single-session-user 0.27, single-session-assistant 0.07 (assistant turns are not candidates for this
extractor).

**Reading.** With weights fitted on the dataset itself and no leakage across questions, the LLM-free
structural gate retains 7 points more gold evidence than random at the same memory size on the second
dataset (and 15 more than the length heuristic), with 500 independent memories as the units. Combined with
LoCoMo (+5.7 over random, 10 clusters), the claim "beats random and the 2010 product at matched size, and
is not a turn-length effect" now rests on two datasets. The hand-set prior weights do not transfer across
datasets (section 8.2); the weights must be fitted per dataset, which the paper must state. The fitted
weights put most mass on the 2010 Impact term and on pattern novelty, so on a 50-session haystack the
"attached to what memory already holds" signal that was useless on LoCoMo carries information here.
